title: Defining AI companions: a research agenda—from artificial companions for learning to general artificial companions for Global Harwell
venue: Research and Practice in Technology Enhanced Learning
extended_summary:
This paper is a conceptual and agenda-setting article that defines AI companions and argues that generative AI is pushing education beyond AI as a mere tool or assistant toward more companion-like systems. The authors distinguish AI tools, assistants, and companions, emphasizing that companions involve mixed initiative interaction and require some form of user model that accounts for intellectual, emotional, social, and value dimensions.

A major focus is the historical development and design logic of artificial learning companions (ALCs). The paper traces the idea back to Chan and Baskin’s learning companions and reviews design approaches such as simulation and machine learning. It then synthesizes prior work on ALC roles, including collaborators, competitors, tutees, negotiators, and animal companions, and links these to educational theories such as Vygotsky’s zone of proximal development, cognitive conflict, cognitive load sharing, and interest-driven creator theory. The paper also highlights AI-related mechanisms relevant to current generative AI, including large language models and retrieval-augmented generation, as well as multimodal, robotic, metaverse, and seamless-learning environments.

The paper does not report an empirical study of a specific student sample or school context. Instead, it proposes a research agenda organized around four questions: emergent technologies, learning theories, educational roles and strategies, and expected outcomes/evaluations. Its main conclusion is that AI companions and ALCs have broad potential to support cognition, metacognition, affect, behavior, social interaction, and wellbeing, but their design and evaluation should be theory-driven, adaptive, and sensitive to the distinct roles companions may play in learning environments.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems and large language models used as adaptive conversational or content-generating educational companions, assistants, or tutoring tools; may include retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for more contextually relevant answers.
identified_tools.use_case: This is a theoretical/review paper on AI companions for learning, discussing how generative AI, LLMs, and RAG could support AI learning companions and educational assistance, including tutoring, feedback, and personalized materials.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/review agenda paper rather than an empirical evaluation of a specific AI tool. It does not report primary data, study design, sample sizes, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues that generative AI and related companion designs may support learning, personalization, and feedback, but it provides no empirical effect sizes or outcome evidence. Impact is therefore speculative and not measurable from this paper.
